name: Metalic Technoforge Limited
summary: Metalic Technoforge is a small, integrated closed-die forging, gear and precision-machining supplier. This is a cyclical manufacturing-growth thesis, not an established compounder. Genuine constant-perimeter revenue growth and better value addition are its strengths; persistent weak cash conversion, customer concentration and the funding burden of a major expansion are the decisive risks. At the official 19 October 2026 close of ₹158.80, the supported base forecast returns 6.10% annualized over five years after 5% exit friction, below the 15% nominal pretax hurdle. BQS 5.5, GQS 5.0 after the cash-conversion cap, and IAS 3.7 imply **Weak setup / value-trap risk**. Better cash conversion, funded commissioning or a materially lower valuation could change this conclusion. No fraud or actual default is inferred. [E01,E05,E08,E28]

factor_audit.what_changes_score: Verified edit logs and competitive RPT procurement help; adverse adjudication or undisclosed benefit would hurt.

factor_audit.rationale: Qualification, tooling and precision integration provide switching friction but custom forging remains competitive and purchase orders not exclusivity.
factor_audit.counterevidence: Repeat customers 89.1% and certifications support stickiness; top customer 22.94% and no LT contracts weaken pricing power.
factor_audit.what_changes_score: Demonstrated customer retention and pricing through cycle, independently verified rejection rates/program life.

factor_audit.rationale: Preselected 3 year comparable organic CAGR 26.76% maps 20–30% band; five years not available. No net trajectory adjustment.
factor_audit.counterevidence: FY26 physical output flat; richer product mix and new customers support economic growth but unit price/volume bridge absent.
factor_audit.what_changes_score: Audited FY27 organic growth, shipped tonnes and value addition; material gross/net restatement could require NS.

factor_audit.rationale: Broader customer base and export/general engineering demand support medium runway; concentration and short order book limit visibility.
factor_audit.counterevidence: No annual guaranteed orders; current capacity 90.22% utilized; delays and European exposure matter.
factor_audit.what_changes_score: Customer program awards, repeat collection and commercialized Unit IV capacity.

factor_audit.rationale: Stable perimeter incremental return 16.98% FY24–26 and 19.20% FY23–26 exceeds 12–15% analyst capital cost, but latest 13.64% and margin-driven bridge temper confidence.
factor_audit.counterevidence: Not project cohort proof; related advances included, idle CWIP /advances retained; IPO cash is not productive capital yet.
factor_audit.what_changes_score: Margin-normalized returns and cash release after commissioning; poor incremental returns would reduce.

factor_audit.rationale: Persistent 3 year CFO / PAT 11.52%, negative FY26 CFO and interest-in-financing leave poor cash realization during profitable growth.
factor_audit.counterevidence: WIP build and expansion explain uses, receivables mostly under 6 months and physical inventory checks positive; not sufficient to excuse three years.
factor_audit.what_changes_score: CFO / PAT above 0.8 over rolling 2 years with interest basis disclosed and without stretched creditors.

factor_audit.rationale: Historic net debt/ EBITDA about 1.43 x and coverage 7.50 x, fresh IPO and known credit line support base; working capital and renewal dependence constrain stress funding.
factor_audit.counterevidence: No actual default; deposits not all free, new capex funds restricted; bear requires counterfactual equity.
factor_audit.what_changes_score: Documented renewal, lower WC, restricted cash use and no incremental unfunded Pune commitment.

factor_audit.rationale: Integrated machining/gear capability, increased customers and obtained licenses demonstrate execution; major expansion not yet tested.
factor_audit.counterevidence: Near flat FY26 tonnes, large new budget and unfinalized Pune proposal; execution cannot be scored as completed.
factor_audit.what_changes_score: On-time Unit IV acceptance, asset-use certification and commercial orders without overruns.

factor_audit.rationale: Revenue, mix and operating margin improvement drive profits; normalized EBIT excludes other income, while per-share progress is lower after actual fresh-capital dilution, on a bonus-adjusted comparable basis.
factor_audit.counterevidence: Other income and FX material, cash weak; actual D&A 4.415 cr not misinferred 1.9793.
factor_audit.what_changes_score: Sustained normalized margin with cash realization and per-share earnings after new capital.

factor_audit.rationale: Base fully funded no-rescue IRR minus 15% hurdle is−8.90 pp, numerical band−10 to−7 pp.
factor_audit.counterevidence: Funding is forecast, not observed current bank balance; no rescue or optional uncommitted factoring used.
factor_audit.what_changes_score: Price and validated operating/funding inputs change model return, not arbitrary score adjustments.

factor_audit.rationale: Credible combined margin/collections/capex delay stress breaches cash floor and may require adverse recapitalization; value can fall materially.
factor_audit.counterevidence: Clean historic default record, existing credit and IPO help base; modeled gap not an actual default.
factor_audit.what_changes_score: Supported stress funding without new external rescue and lower cash-cycle dependence.

factor_audit.rationale: 158.80 requires multiple optimistic operating assumptions or≈18.7 x terminal EBITDA for 15% hurdle; base 12 x produces 6.10%.
factor_audit.counterevidence: Funded bull can exceed hurdle, but requires more rich mix, utilization, cash conversion and 16 x exit valuation.
factor_audit.what_changes_score: Lower price or stronger funded cash flows without multiple expansion.

evidence.claim: FY26 main opinion and IFC unmodified; CARO no fraud/default/wilful default or≥10% inventory count discrepancy.

evidence.claim: Quarterly bank returns differ; FY26 Q2 inventory books 26.4443 vsbank 24.5461 cr,7.18% gap; Q4 stock and debtors match.

evidence.claim: FY26 audited PAT 12.1816→restated 12.3644 cr,1.50% adjustment explained by tax/deferred tax/ MSME interest/rent. CFO identical.

evidence.claim: FY24–26 attributable aggregate incremental NOPAT /operating capital 16.98%; FY23–26≈19.20%; latest one-year≈13.64%.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Margin/mix improvement contributes heavily; not a verified project cohort IRR or perpetual ROIC.

evidence.claim: FY26 RPT expense 4.1304 cr,4.32% of revenue; related capital goods purchases FY24–25≈5.875 cr.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Auditor ordinary course/arm's length statement is not independent competitive price validation.

evidence.claim: Auditor Hetal Patel resigned 1 Aug 2025, stated preoccupation in other assignments; MB Jajodia appointed 28 Aug 2025.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: No disclosed disagreement identified; cannot call entire history no resignation.

evidence.claim: Promoter 61% post IPO; issuer GST scrutiny 23 Jul 2026 unquantified; promoter former partnership GST allegation remains not adjudicated issuer fraud.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Retirement deed 10 Jul does not provide regulatory exoneration; allegations not proven misconduct. Public cutoff pledge confirmation ND.

evidence.claim: Completed all-fresh IPO 6,488,000 shares@77 gross 49.9576 cr, expenses 6.4903, net 43.4673; no OFS.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Board allotment 24 July; model July 28 receipt availability assumed and delayed 14/30 daysstressed.

evidence.claim: IPO uses capex 30.8113 cr, CC / EPC repayment 6.72, GCP 5.936;0.27 cr expenses already internally deployed by July 24 and recoupable.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Remaining external fees 6.2203 on receipt,0.27 prepaid cash July 24 assumption. Prior-March prepayment 0–0.27 sensitivity; no double counted reimbursement.

evidence.claim: June 30 debt 29.3239 cr: CC / EPC 14.4692, term/promoter 14.4225, factoring 0.4322; CC sanction 14.5.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Factoring limit 5 cr not unconditional cash headroom; eligible buyers/invoices required. Renewal not guaranteed.

evidence.claim: Unit IV planned commission 31 Mar 2028; capacity 6800→8800 tonnes; IPO capital budget spent FY27 does not imply FY27 new production.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Base adds new output FY29, bear FY30; quotes exclude taxes/freight etc, overrun and GST modeled.

evidence.claim: 25 Sep Pune leased facility/machinery proposal board approved; cost and commercial terms not final.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: No commissioned capacity or completed acquisition claimed; baseline excludes upside,5/10 cr unfunded cost stress included.

evidence.claim: Published March cash 0.3614 cr; FD 1.6701 cr not treated as free; debt 31.781 includes current term maturities once.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Model is dated forecast from published cash and known IPO, not asserted actual 20 Oct bank balance.

evidence.claim: Old net tax 3.1042 cr, statutory 0.1105, MSME interest 0.0478, contingent TDS 0.057663197, gratuity 0.5632 and capital commitment 1.1762 separately modeled.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Net old tax not offset twice by tax assets;0.8620 tax asset and 0.0044 FD interest recoveries zero base, bounded upside.

evidence.claim: 58 eligible postlisting official sessions all present; 2 earlier calendar sessions prelisting NA. 19 Octclose 158.80.
evidence.locator: dated issuer row/validated daily NSE pay loads
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: No current rolling quote substituted; official historic spread/depth unavailable.

evidence.claim: 20 day mean/median 12.715528/12.621560 million INR;58 day mean/median 24.934084/16.049640 million;1600 lot costs 254080.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: 5% whole lot capacity 3 lots/day is not execution guarantee; Stseriesand 5% band restrict trading.

evidence.claim: Funded base forecast generates low 6.10% five-year IRR at 158.80 after 5% exit friction; 15% hurdle entry≈106.14.
evidence.locator: model dated cash ledger and base case
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Assumes normal CC renewal, lower Wcdays, successful Unit IV, mix growth and 12 x exit multiple. Not a guarantee or automatic buy price.

evidence.claim: Bear no-rescue cash floor breach pre entry/ FY27; no ordinary bear IRR. Equity rescue fees, dilution, dated prefunding explicit and not committed.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Hypothetical pre entry rescue changes actual known share count, thus cannot describe actual issuer history.

evidence.claim: At 15% hurdle base operations require≈18.7 x terminal EV/ EBITDA, versus 12 x base; growth-only solver has no funded crossing.
evidence.locator: reverse expectations and funded multiple bracket
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Higher growth also requires WC/capacity; no fake endpoint reported as solution.

evidence.claim: Peer financial comparison Amic/Tirupati/Paramount is issuer reported FY26; profit mix and end markets differ.
evidence.locator: S 01 pp 132–135; Amic official about page
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: July 23 peer quotes not cutoff quotes; no industry average 77 x P/E used as fair value.

evidence.claim: Factory II / III licenses obtained 4 May 2026; prior integration and output observable but Unit IV /Pune pending.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Prior output near full capacity limits volume upside before expansion.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Metalic Technoforge is a small, integrated closed-die forging, gear and precision-machining supplier. This is a cyclical manufacturing-growth thesis, not an established compounder. Genuine constant-perimeter revenue growth and better value addition are its strengths; persistent weak cash conversion, customer concentration and the funding burden of a major expansion are the decisive risks. At the official 19 October 2026 close of ₹158.80, the supported base forecast returns 6.10% annualized over five years after 5% exit friction, below the 15% nominal pretax hurdle. BQS 5.5, GQS 5.0 after the cash-conversion cap, and IAS 3.7 imply **Weak setup / value-trap risk**. Better cash conversion, funded commissioning or a materially lower valuation could change this conclusion. No fraud or actual default is inferred. [E01,E05,E08,E28]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company earns on customer-specific forged and machined components, including gears, shafts, hydraulic and construction parts. It buys steel, develops dies/tooling, forges and heat-treats blanks, machines or finishes them, and sells to OEM and engineering customers. Customer qualification and finishing content affect economics more than forging tonnes alone. Working capital is absorbed from steel through work-in-progress and finished goods to receivables; jobwork, scrap and inventory movement complicate any simple tonnes-times-price identity. Gross profit is not disclosed on a reliably comparable basis; revenue less materials and inventory movement is only a value-added proxy, not a fabricated gross-margin figure. [E02,E04,E07,E09]

 FY26 product revenue mix was gears 46.23%, general engineering 31.82%, hydraulic 9.38%, construction 7.16%, scrap 4.04% and jobwork 1.37%. The separate end-use classification was agriculture 29.62%, general engineering 21.51%, oil/gas 12%, hydraulic 9.05%, automotive 6.30%, construction 7.16%, gearbox 4.50% and others 9.85%; these are different classifications, not additive segment totals. Rajkot I supports forging/heat treatment, II machining/gears, III tooling/stores, while leased Unit IV is planned. Certifications include IATF 16949, ISO 14001/45001 and PED /AD 2000; the claimed DIN 5 gear capability and 1 MW solar saving 40–60% of power are issuer assertions, not independent moat proof. [E02]

 FY26 exports were ₹33.8237 crore,35.40% of sales, versus ₹28.0530 crore in FY25 and ₹9.4438 crore in FY24. Germany alone represented 20.61% of FY26 sales; US exposure 5.33%, down from 9.25%. The company reports no currency hedging. Repeat-customer revenue rose from ₹34.4241 crore to ₹85.1303 crore across FY24–26; these are repeat orders, not contracted subscriptions. [E03,E06]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible moat is qualification, component-specific tooling, dimensional consistency and integration from forging to precision machining. A safety-critical qualified part can be costly to switch, but the report finds no exclusive long-duration purchase commitment, proprietary product monopoly or quantified switching cost. Certifications are often entry tickets in this market. Supplier relationships and technical reputation support MOAT 5, not a premium brand or market-share claim. [E02,E03]

Top-customer exposure was 22.94% in FY26, down from 24.89% in FY25 and 30.53% in FY24. Top five 45.35% and top ten 64.61% still create meaningful bargaining and utilization risk. Customer count rose 98→126→181; new customer count 38/60/79 over FY24/25/26 suggests genuine demand access. The ₹27.6115 crore order book at 30 June is intended for 1–3 months, not multi year backlog, with no full intake/cancellation/collection rollforward. [E03]

Issuer-reported FY26 peer comparisons are Amic Forging revenue ₹141.7848 crore/ EBITDA margin 30.16%, Tirupati Forge ₹162.4785 crore/9.76%, and Paramount Speciality Forgings ₹119.9597 crore/6.24%, against Metalic ₹95.5475 crore/22.97%. Amic’s official description includes open forging and heavy industrial precision components, making it an imperfect closed-die/machining peer. Balance-sheet leverage, other income and product mix differ. July 23 peer P/Es 64.85/151.92/14.38 are not current cutoff valuations; their arithmetic average is not fair value. No verified sector market-share or consistent sector organic-growth series was found, so no out performance bonus is awarded. [E31]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Unit IV is a substantial reinvestment rather than a capital-free extension. Existing capacity 6,800 tonnes is already 90.22% utilized. The disclosed project targets 8,800 tonnes plus gear, heat-treatment and testing capabilities. Budget deployment in FY27 is not commercial production in FY27: construction/installation extends through 2027 and target commissioning is 31 March 2028. Base recognizes incremental production in FY29; bear delays it to FY30. Quoted costs exclude taxes/import/freight items, so base adds 10% capex overrun and temporary 18% GST cash, with delayed credit recovery. [E22]

The dated IPO provides ₹30.8113 crore of eligible capital earmarks, not a freely distributable balance. Maintenance capex continues at 2% of revenue in base, growth working capital is funded, existing capital commitment ₹1.1762 crore is retained separately to avoid assuming overlap, and later bull capacity increases require additional capex. Bull FY30 ₹2 crore precedes FY31+400 tonnes; FY31 ₹6 crore precedes FY32 another 400 tonnes; FY32 ₹4 crore is ongoing capital with no additional capacity credited yet. No Pune production is credited: September 25 approval had unfinalized terms and price. Its ₹5/10 crore cash stress adds no earnings. [E20,E23,E25]

 FY24–26 incremental NOPAT rose ₹8.03 crore on ₹47.31 crore incremental operating capital, a 16.98% return versus 12–15% analyst capital cost. The arithmetic scale contribution at FY24 operating margin is ₹3.86 crore(8.16% incremental return); ₹4.17 crore is mix/margin/operating-leverage residual, not separately identified causal improvement. FY23–26 full incremental return is 19.20%; latest one-year is 13.64%. This supports CAP 6, not indefinite high ROIC. Uncommissioned assets, advances and related party capital remain in the denominator. [E15]

 GQS raw 6.35 is capped 5.00 because persistent CASH 3 undermines the otherwise strong revenue growth. It would be wrong both to deny genuine organic growth and to call it cash-generative compounding before collections and WIP funding improve. [E08,E09]

Promoters retain 61.00% post IPO. Alignment from ownership is offset by related-party procurement and execution concentration, not automatically negated by them. Related-party expenses were ₹4.1304 crore/4.32% of FY26 revenue, versus ₹5.5693 crore/7.49% in FY25 and ₹4.2078 crore/8.27% in FY24. Related capital goods purchases were ₹3.3104 crore in FY25 and ₹2.5646 crore in FY24, principally Motiontech Solution LLP; these are asset purchases, not a newly consolidated acquired company. Auditors describe ordinary-course/arm’s-length compliance, but no independent price tender comparison is available. FY26 managerial remuneration ₹0.99 crore and related salaries ₹0.7786 crore should be monitored against profit and productive contribution. [E16,E18]

Hetal Patel resigned 1 August 2025 with the stated reason preoccupation in other assignments. MB Jajodia was appointed 28 August and regularized 30 September 2025. The FY25 CARO resignation clause is preserved; there is no identified disclosed audit disagreement, and no claim that resignation never occurred. [E17]

The issuer received a GST scrutiny notice 23 July 2026 relating to FY23 differences/short payment/input credit, with amount unquantified and reply pending. A separate GST allegation concerned a promoter’s former partnership; retirement 10 July 2026 is not regulatory exoneration, but allegations are not established issuer misconduct. The TDS contingent demand ₹0.057663197 crore is identified separately. Current promoter pledge confirmation is ND, not zero. [E18,E25]

Normalized NOPAT uses 29.12% tax and excludes other income. Forecast operating invested capital and incremental-return denominators retain unrecovered project GST credits until cash recovery, even though these credits sit outside ordinary working-capital days. Current ROIC uses average capital; incremental ROIC uses changes in NOPAT and capital over stated periods. The financing-capital reconciliation residual is attributable to excluded tax/statutory/gratuity items, not silently forced to zero. [E15,E24,E25]

Bonus 16:1 in March 2026 changes units, not economic dilution. FY25 rights capital ₹0.65 crore, FY26 pre bonus private placement 29,200 shares at ₹1,250 gross ₹3.65 crore, and IPO 6,488,000 fresh shares add real capital and dilute per-share claims. Restated weighted EPS FY24/25/26 about ₹7.17/₹6.93/₹7.12 is not current EPS: FY26 PAT on 23,984,400 current shares is ₹5.1552, normalized ex-other-income EPS about ₹4.49. No outstanding convertibles were identified in the prospectus. [E01,E19]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹158.80, equity market cap is ₹380.872272 crore, reported FY26 P/E on current post IPO shares≈30.80 x and normalized ex-other income P/E≈35.36 x. These are historical profit multiples on current capital, not weighted pre IPO EPS multiples. March debt is not called current debt; post IPO valuation uses the dated cash/debt bridge below. No operating property value is added a second time and no NCI /subsidiary value is assumed. [E01,E07,E19,E24]

The primary method is funded earnings EV-to-equity at 20 October 2031. DCF and normalized P/E are cross checks, not a claimed precise target. Forecasts model capacity×utilization×blended revenue/production, margin, tax, D&A, working capital, maintenance/project capex, debt interest/principal, earmarks, old claims and cash reserve. The base DCF cross-check is ₹119.90 per current share at a 14% discount rate and 12× terminal EV/ EBITDA. Terminal value contributes 87.09% of discounted firm value, so this is heavily exit-dependent, not a precise intrinsic value. The 12%/14%/16% discount-rate and 8×/12×/16× terminal-multiple matrix spans ₹78.35–₹168.61 per share. The normalized P/E cross-check is ₹187.59 at the terminal date using 18× earnings, not a present-day target. [E28–E30]

₹0.25 crore minimum cash is an analyst reserve, not a regulatory minimum or actual distress point; reserves 0/0.25/1/2 are stressed. Exit 5% friction is not claimed as an observed spread;2/5/10% are tested. No dividends are assumed. [E22,E24–E30]

Unfunded bear terminal value is an asset-earnings diagnostic, not an executable investor return. Separate rescue bear generates-14.13%, ₹9.38 crore net new capital and 4.14% total dilution versus current known shares; its pre entry share issue is explicitly counterfactual. It does not claim the actual October register changed. Base and bull need no equity rescue under their stated assumptions.

Base funding begins with March cash ₹0.3614 crore and debt ₹31.781 crore, incorporates June actual debt ₹29.3239 crore, completed IPO gross ₹49.9576 crore and fees ₹6.4903 crore once. ₹0.27 crore internally deployed IPO expenses are assumed paid 24 July; only ₹6.2203 crore external fees on receipt, with reimbursement embedded in retained cash rather than added again. Known share allotment adds 6,488,000 shares on 24 July, independently of cash availability. IPO availability 28 July is an assumption anchored to allotment/listing, tested 14/30 days later; these cash delays do not move the legal allotment date. Pre-receipt cash is checked before crediting IPO receipts. The legal earmark ₹30.8113 crore funds only eligible project uses; ₹6.72 crore pays CC / EPC, not term loans; ₹5.936 crore is general purpose. [E19,E20]

The ₹14.5 crore existing CC / EPC sanction is the maximum revolver, with normal renewal assumed; its removal is tested. Factoring ₹5 crore limit requires eligible buyer/invoices and is not cash available on request; base uses no additional factoring. Term repayment assumptions are ₹4.5/4.5/3.5/1.9225 crore FY27–30 following June, with ₹0.4322 crore factoring repaid FY27; exact contractual amortization remains ND, so this is not a verified maturity schedule. Cash interest uses opening debt over elapsed intervals; new draws prefund uses and include incremental interest, rather than using end-period IPO repayment to erase earlier interest. [E21]

Old net tax ₹3.1042 crore, statutory ₹0.1105, MSME interest ₹0.0478 and TDS contingency ₹0.057663197 are settled once; gratuity ₹0.5632 is paid progressively. Tax assets ₹0.8620 plus accrued FD interest ₹0.0044 are explicitly zero-recovery base, not silently offset again against the net tax provision. Deposits ₹1.6701 are not free base cash; documented pledge ₹0.75 means at most ₹0.9201 is tested as an upper bound, not assumed released. Operating leases remain rent cost; no unsupported Ind AS lease debt is added. [E24,E25]

Exact entry free cash is ₹2.27 crore, earmark ₹20.64 crore, debt ₹21.10 crore in the base forecast, not observed current balances. Signed entry cash after reserve is ₹2.02; the terminal reserve stays with operations, not distributed twice. Only cash flows until 20 October 2031 enter investor returns; FY32 full-year earnings are an explicit terminal run-rate assumption, not post-terminal cash funding.

A growth-only reverse grid−5% to 40% finds no funded bracket crossing at 12/15/18% hurdles; no end point is reported as a solution. The fixed-operations multiple solver has a finite funded 4–40 x bracket and tiny residual; attaining 15% requires about 18.7 x versus 12 x base. [E28,E30]

Growth override rows are demand diagnostics that may require extra capacity or value addition, not automatic physical forecasts. Full annual and dated rows are preserved with funding flags. sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is that recent profit growth reflects mix and inventory absorption rather than repeatable cash unit economics. A top customer slowdown or European industrial downturn can reduce utilization while WIP, tooling and receivables remain funded. Unit IV overruns and delays then consume IPO earmarks before commissioning; CC renewal or invoice eligibility weakness removes the working capital bridge. This is a linked operating/funding problem, not merely a lower exit multiple. [E03,E04,E08,E09,E21,E22]

The bear assumes 17–18% margin, DSO 115–120 days initially, higher inventories, lower creditor financing,20% project overrun and FY30 new capacity. It breaches the ₹0.25 crore analyst cash floor before entry and later FY27, maximum unrescued gap ₹9.45 crore. Ordinary bear IRR and entry prices are therefore null even if later cash becomes positive. The model does not fund an earlier hole with later IPO or FY32 cash. Its terminal diagnostic ₹77.51 implies about 51.19% price impairment before exit cost, but actual outcome could be worse if no financing is available. [E29]

Explicit rescue issues whole external shares at 40% discount to ₹158.80 with 5% fees, net cash received before interval uses. Capital raising is not committed, rescue holders are distinct from the incumbent, and no incumbent rights contribution is silently assumed. Pre entry rescue changes hypothetical entry shares; post entry ownership dilution is separately reported. The fact that real IPO completed and no financial default is reported prevents treating this hypothetical bear as actual distress. G3 remains Conditional, D 3 captures the loss risk. [E19,E21,E29]

Thesis-break variables are receivable/ WIP cash release, incremental unit value addition and commissioning without unfunded cost. Absence of reliable edit logs or new material unexplained bank/financial mismatches would also change G2, unlike an explained classification difference. [E11–E15]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A fivefold share price from ₹158.80 requires ₹794 and tenfold ₹1,588, corresponding to 37.97% and 58.49% annualized over five years before friction. At unchanged current shares these imply equity values ₹1,904.36 crore and ₹3,808.72 crore, before any rescue or new growth capital. The funded bull terminal price is far below 5×, even with higher capacity, richer product mix,24% margin and 16 x exit EBITDA. No audited customer program, capacity path and cash financing supports 5×/10×as a base claim. The business may grow well without the entry valuation delivering multibagger returns. [E22,E28–E30]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
**Weak setup / value-trap risk**, using unrounded BQS 5.46 and IAS 3.665. The business is not rejected for proven fraud, but is not a compounder: GOV / MOAT / DUR / CAP are below 7, CASH below 6, BQS below 8 and GQS capped 5. At ₹158.80 the base 6.10% return is not adequate for the identified risks. This supports a research watchlist/avoid-new-entry conclusion under the stated framework, not an instruction for an existing holder. [E08,E15,E28–E30]

A price closer to ₹106.14 would satisfy the 15% hurdle only if base cash flows, funding, commissioning and exit 12 x remain credible. A lower price cannot cure audit controls, lost customers or unfunded capex. Upgrades need cash realization and verified project returns; downgrades follow adverse governance evidence, material unreconciled accounts, or actual unfinanceability. All numeric rankings are conditionally eligible because critical gates are not failed/held and all factors scoreable; IAS is explicitly for the illustrative ₹5 lakh reference, not individualized suitability. [E10–E15,E19–E30]
